hook.line: Vale's mother wants to know about everyone, and soon you'll be asked about your family too. Spanish has one short word for a mixed group, and it's the one you'd use for brothers.
hook.es: Mis papás y mis hermanos viven en Medellín.
hook.en: My parents and my brothers and sisters live in Medellín.

examples.en: My brothers and sisters live in Cali.
My aunts and uncles live in Bogotá.
Do your grandparents live in Toronto? (to a friend)

rule:
When a group mixes men and women, Spanish uses the -os form:

*mis hermanos* = my brothers and sisters
*mis papás* = my parents (mum and dad)
*mis tíos* = my aunts and uncles
*mis abuelos* = my grandparents

The -as form is only for a group of women: *mis hermanas* = my sisters.

So *Tengo tres hermanos* tells you how many, not who. Three brothers, or two sisters and a brother: same words. If it matters, people ask *¿Hombres o mujeres?*

In Colombia *mis papás* is the everyday way to say my parents; *mis padres* is a little more formal.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the generic masculine (masculino genérico): the masculine plural stands for a mixed group.

options: My brothers and sisters live in Cali.
My aunts and uncles are very nice.
Do your cousins (men and women) speak English? (to a friend)
Do your cousins (all women) speak English? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Los nietos de Hernando viven en Bogotá.

options: My aunts and uncles have a café.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *hermanos* or *hermanas* (two brothers and a sister): Tengo tres ___.
yourTurn.why: One man in the group is enough for *hermanos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tíos* or *tías* (all of them are women): Mis ___ viven en Cali.
yourTurn.why: A group of women only, so *tías*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: My parents live in Bogotá. Use the everyday Colombian word.
yourTurn.why: Mum plus dad makes *papás*, the -s form of *papá*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: My grandparents are from Boyacá.
Ask a friend: Do you have brothers or sisters?
yourTurn.why: *Hermanos* covers brothers, sisters or both, so one word does the job.

yourTurn.prompt: Your aunt has a husband. Make it about both of them: Mi tía vive en Medellín.
yourTurn.why: Aunt plus uncle is *tíos*, and *vive* becomes *viven*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about all your cousins, men and women: Mi prima es muy divertida.
yourTurn.why: A mixed group takes -os everywhere: *primos* and *divertidos*.

pitfalls.wrong: Pablo y Ana son mis hermanas.
pitfalls.right: Pablo y Ana son mis hermanos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Pablo is a man, so the group is *hermanos*; *hermanas* means sisters only.
*Parientes* means relatives. Your parents are *mis papás*.
The describing word follows the group: several people, so *simpáticos*.

personal: Write two lines about the groups in your family: your parents, brothers and sisters, grandparents or cousins. Use *mis papás*, *mis hermanos* or *mis abuelos*, and say where they live.
